Here are a handful of *low‑stress, crowd‑pleasing* contributions you can bring to a 25‑30‑person gathering. They come straight from the “Elevated Event Menu” notes (see [[summaries/session-08_2024-06-12]]) and are flagged with the **make‑ahead** tag [[concepts/make-ahead-cooking]].

| Item (what to bring) | Why it’s easy & popular | Quick prep / make‑ahead notes |
|----------------------|------------------------|--------------------------------|
| **Citrus‑ginger mocktail (batch beverage)** | Refreshing, non‑alcoholic, looks fancy in a 2‑gal dispenser, and can be pre‑mixed the night before. | Mix 48 oz citrus juice, 24 oz ginger syrup, 32 oz cranberry juice, and fill the rest with still water — store chilled. Add sparkling water only at serving time [[summaries/session-08_2024-06-12]]. |
| **Marinated olives & mixed nuts platter** | No cooking required, instantly edible, and a classic “snack‑able” starter that satisfies salty cravings. | Buy 1.5 lb olives and 1 lb mixed nuts (or a bit more for 30 guests). Toss olives with a splash of olive oil, lemon zest, and herbs; keep nuts in a bowl. Both can sit out on a simple serving board all evening [[summaries/session-08_2024-06-12]]. |
| **Farro‑vegetable salad (make‑ahead grain salad)** | Hearty, gluten‑friendly, and can be served cold or at room temperature—no reheating needed. | Cook 3 lb dry farro (≈1 qt) the day before, roast 6 lb assorted vegetables (e.g., carrots, bell peppers, zucchini), and whisk a dressing of 1 cup olive oil + ½ cup lemon juice. Cool farro and veg, then store separately; toss together with dressing just before serving [[summaries/session-08_2024-06-12]]. |
| **Warm bite pieces (mini tart squares or stuffed‑mushroom caps)** | Small, savory finger foods that look elegant but require only a short bake on the day. | Prepare 50‑60 bite‑size pieces (e.g., puff‑pastry squares filled with cheese & herbs, or mushroom caps stuffed with sautéed onion, mushroom bits, and cheese). Bake them the night before, let cool, and re‑heat 5‑10 min in a 350 °F oven right before guests arrive [[summaries/session-08_2024-06-12]]. |

### How to keep it stress‑free
1. **Batch everything the day before** – the mocktail base, farro and roasted veggies, olives, nuts, and even the bite pieces can all be prepared ahead of time.  
2. **Minimal on‑the‑day tasks** – reheat only the bite pieces; the salad is assembled at the last minute; the mocktail just gets sparkling water added.  
3. **Simple plating** – a large pitcher for the mocktail, a rustic board for olives & nuts, a big bowl for the farro salad, and a tray for the warm bites. No elaborate serviceware needed.

Pick any 1‑2 of these items (or all four if you feel generous) and you’ll contribute tasty, crowd‑pleasing food without spending the entire day in the kitchen. Enjoy the gathering!
